concurrency_primitives: goroutine per dataset + WaitGroup; reader->bounded batch channel->N parser goroutines->ordered collector (ingest/csvstream.go:129-222); generic ParallelReduce/ParallelFor with private accumulators (join/parallel.go); 3 spatial grids built in parallel and 3 joins in parallel (join/join.go:46-125); 5 analyses concurrent with recover (analysis.go:36-55); fetch worker pool + single writer goroutine with context cancellation (fetch.go:191-273); RWMutex interner; atomic memory sampler; sync.Pool
design_patterns: Pipeline (pipeline.Run stages), Builder (pipeline.Builder with validation), Factory (ingest.NewSource, report.NewRenderer), Strategy (analysis.Question, report.Renderer)
questions: Which neighborhoods face compounded distress across public safety, housing and city services? (Crime+Vacants+311+Liquor)
Is violent crime concentrated around liquor outlets, and which outlets stand out? (Liquor+Crime+311 baseline, spatial)
Do vacant buildings drive trash, dumping and rodent complaints, and where is demand out of line with vacancy? (Vacants+311)
Are 311 requests from high-crime neighborhoods resolved as quickly as elsewhere? (311+Crime, mix-adjusted)
When, and around which places, should late-night patrol and outreach be concentrated? (Crime+Liquor)
stakeholders: Board of Liquor License Commissioners & Baltimore Police Department
Department of Public Works & Department of Housing and Community Development
BPD Patrol Command & Mayor's Office of Neighborhood Safety and Engagement
overview: A polished standard-library Go pipeline in 11 internal packages (ingest, join, spatial, stats, analysis, report, pipeline, fetch, sample, model) driven by a Makefile and a Builder-validated CLI. Parsing streams CSV through batched worker pools with ordered collection, joins use a spatial grid and generic sharded reducers, five Question strategies run concurrently, and a renderer-neutral report tree is emitted to terminal, Markdown, HTML and CSV. Code is idiomatic, well-commented and covered by 25 tests including determinism and end-to-end checks; the README matches the code exactly.
stakeholder_value: On the synthetic default the findings merely recover the generator's planted relationships. On fetched real 2022 data, Q1 (composite distress), Q3 (vacancy vs sanitation residuals) and Q4 (mix-adjusted 311 wait by crime tercile, per-agency gaps) give the Mayor's Office, DPW/DHCD and DOT genuinely actionable rankings; Q2 fails and Q5's outlet comparison is empty because the live Liquor Licenses layer carries no coordinates through this fetcher.
issues: No real data bundled; documented Quick Start (make demo) and the submitted report.html use a synthetic generator with planted relationships (clearly labeled)
Live fetch of Liquor Licenses returns blank X/Y (and 12,499 of 30,953 IDs), so all licenses are dropped as no_location; Q2 returns an error section and Q5's near-outlet share is 0.0% on real data
Real-data run yields 3 of 5 answers cleanly
311 is sampled to 150k of ~1M rows by default (documented)
No unit tests for analysis, report, sample packages
rationale: Full marks for build, concurrency, memory design, architecture and README reflect a clean, race-free, well-tested multi-package Go system. Real-data scoring follows the rubric for runtime-only fetching with a mock default (10-3=7), and stakeholder/runs are trimmed because the liquor-dependent questions cannot be answered on live data even though the synthetic path completes. 87/100, B.
